1) Deletion SLA: we are targeting a contractual requirement that customer data be removed from production and backups within 30 days of request. This includes snapshots and any backup media that could be used to restore deleted data.

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear questions. Happy to provide technical detail here and we can walk the SRE call through specifics. TL;DR: we can meet a 30-day deletion SLA for customer data including backups, with the caveats below.

Details:
- Primary data: when a deletion request is issued (via API or contract escalation), primary datastore entries are removed within 48 hours. Deletion is logical + asynchronous background compaction where applicable.
- Backups / snapshots: Redwood maintains encrypted backups and periodic snapshots for disaster recovery. For customers contracting a 30-day deletion SLA we:
  * Mark customer data for expedited purging from backup index and restore catalogs;
  * Ensure that any automated snapshot retention windows do not prevent removal — snapshots that would otherwise keep data for longer are either deleted or rekeyed so data cannot be restored.
  * Typical operational window for irreversible removal from backups: up to 30 days, depending on snapshot cadence. We plan the contract to guarantee removal within 30 days.
- Immutable snapshots: where immutable snapshoting is used for security, we can apply an exception process for contracted customers so that the immutable window will not block deletion of customer data; this is handled as an operational runbook item and reflected in the agreement.
- Log retention: default platform retention for audit/access logs is 90 days. We can configure retention to 30/90/365 days by route, and we support exporting logs to a customer-managed logging endpoint (e.g., S3 / Splunk) if you need longer retention under your control. Logs are redacted for PII by default and are encrypted at rest.
- SOC 2: we host the report behind an NDA. I attached our short product sheet with the retention and deletion bullets (redwood-data-retention-ps.pdf) and added a link to SOC 2 access.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-ps.pdf

If helpful, we can provide a short sequence diagram on the SRE call showing how primary delete triggers backup purge steps. Proposed times for the call: Tue/Wed next week 10-12 PT.

Hi Dana / team —

Adding the security/compliance perspective. We can support Amaya's requirements; a few process notes: 

1) SOC 2 access: we require an NDA before we share the Type II report. Once NDA is in place, procurement will receive a link with a time-limited view. Typical turnaround: 1 business day after NDA execution.
2) Vendor security questionnaire: if you return the XLS we will triage internally. For high-risk items we aim for 3-5 business day responses; for the full questionnaire expect up to 10 business days for thorough evidence collection depending on the number of attachments requested.
3) HIPAA / BA: Redwood will sign a BA where PHI is in scope. Our standard BA template is attached (redwood-ba-template.pdf). BA execution requires legal review and signatures from both sides — estimate 2-3 weeks once both parties engage legal.
4) Evidence for backups and deletion: we will provide our deletion runbook excerpts and operational controls as evidence. For customers requiring 30-day deletion from backups, we include explicit contract language and an operational playbook to ensure compliance.

Proposed next steps (agreed timeline):
- Amaya to confirm target deletion SLA (30 days?) and whether PHI will be in scope.
- Amaya to return the vendor security questionnaire with any marked "must-have" items this week.
- Redwood to return a majority of questionnaire answers within 3 business days, and the remaining evidence within 10 business days.
- Schedule SRE call for technical walkthrough (Marissa to propose slots).

Happy to join the call.

Best,
